extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in marketing, journalism, and digital content (editors, social media managers, content strategists)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate or design news/online articles to maximize email- or social-sharing based on psychological and content features identified in Berger & Milkman (2012). Focuses on emotional drivers, content characteristics, and editorial placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physiological arousal
rubrics_metrics.description: Virality is partially driven by physiological arousal: content that evokes high arousal is more likely to be shared than low-arousal content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-arousal emotions (regardless of valence) increase sharing. The paper finds that arousal accounts for a substantial portion of sharing variance; design content to elicit strong, immediate emotional responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-arousal positive emotions (awe)
rubrics_metrics.description: High-arousal positive states—most notably awe—increase virality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awe-inspiring content (e.g., scientific discoveries, stories of overcoming adversity, transcendence or inspiration) is especially likely to be shared. Emphasize inspirational framing and extraordinary achievements to boost shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-arousal negative emotions (anger)
rubrics_metrics.description: High-arousal negative emotions such as anger or outrage drive sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content that provokes indignation or moral outrage is likely to be forwarded; craft headlines and narratives that highlight perceived injustices or strong normative violations to elicit anger-driven sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-arousal negative emotions (anxiety/fear)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anxiety or threat-related high-arousal negative emotions increase sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that signal threat, urgency, or fear can prompt sharing—especially when readers feel compelled to warn or mobilize others. Use salient stakes and imminent consequences to raise arousal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-arousal emotions (sadness) reduce sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Low-arousal emotions—especially sadness—are associated with lower likelihood of sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sad, melancholic, or low-energy negative stories are less viral. If covering sad topics, consider framing elements that increase arousal (e.g., surprise, inspiration) to counteract low sharing propensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valence (positivity vs. negativity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive content is more viral than negative content when controlling for arousal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When arousal level is similar, positively valenced pieces (e.g., uplifting surprises, inspirational stories) tend to be shared more than negative ones. Favor positive-framed angles if comparable arousal can be achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise / unexpectedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Surprising content—elements that violate expectations or present the unexpected—predicts higher sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use unexpected facts, counterintuitive findings, or surprising twists in storytelling to raise arousal and curiosity, increasing share likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility (actionable information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practically useful, actionable content (tips, how-tos, serviceable information) predicts virality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, usable takeaways or steps readers can apply; content that helps readers solve problems or act is more frequently forwarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest / curiosity gap
rubrics_metrics.description: Content that creates an information gap or strong curiosity (interestingness) is more likely to be shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ curiosity gaps in headlines and openings (what readers don't know but want to learn) to raise interest and prompt sharing for social currency or self-presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominently featured placement (editorial promotion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Placement and editorial prominence amplify sharing: prominently featured items are more likely to be shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decision-making and homepage/section placement materially affect virality; combine strong content features with prominent placement to maximize reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-pattern: boring or purely utilitarian without emotional hook
rubrics_metrics.description: Boring, strictly utilitarian content that lacks an emotional hook tends to be less viral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid purely informational or dry presentations without arousal-inducing framing; even practical pieces benefit from an emotional or surprising angle to increase sharing.
